messages:
maria (oncall): seeing a sharp spike in controller-manager leader renewer errors and concurrent GPU attach failures in eu-central1. apiserver returning 503s for brief windows. any ideas?

deploy-bot: rollout eu-central1/model-serving-v2 completed at 2026-03-20T01:12:04Z (canary -> 50%).

maria (oncall): timeline: errors started ~01:12 UTC right after the canary. logs show leader renewer RPC timeouts and etcd write latencies.

jon (sre): pulling metrics now. etcd commit latency jumped and leader changed twice in 30s. watch compact and snapshot IOs are peaking. probable IO stall causing leader churn -> apiserver watch/backoff -> controller queue pileup.

kai (infra): checked node attach logs for GPU pool: lots of attach retries 504/timeout, CNI flaps reported, NAT conn counts spiking in euc1-nat. Could be egress saturating during snapshot writes.

maria (oncall): paste of controller-manager snippet: ```Mar 20 01:12:14 controller-manager[1]: WARN controller-runtime.manager.leader: lease renewer error: rpc error: code=Unavailable desc=transport is closing```

amelia (eng-runtime): fwiw the rollout increased concurrency to 600 rps on some routes. autoscaler reacted and started burst provisioning GPUs which caused heavy disk/snapshot churn on the same region. coupling looks suspicious.

jon (sre): hypothesis: burst provision -> many nodes attach -> kubelet/attach-controller heavy calls -> etcd snapshot/compaction IO contention -> leader jitter -> apiserver 5xx -> controllers stall -> more retries -> provisioner thrash. feedback loop.

kai (infra): immediate mitigations we can try: 1) pause the canary rollback/scale (canary -> 0%), 2) increase controller-manager leader-election lease duration from 15s -> 45s temporarily, 3) set provisioning cooldown to 180s for GPU pool in eu-central1. Which do we want now?

maria (oncall): start with pausing canary + provisioning cooldown. I'll also increase lease duration to 40s to avoid fast leader flips.

maria (oncall): rolling actions: `kubectl -n redwood rollout pause deployment/model-serving-canary-euc1` -> done.

kai (infra): applied pool cooldown: `infractl pools update eu-central1-gpu --scale-cooldown=180` -> accepted.

kai (infra): bumped controller-manager args on control plane nodes: `--leader-elect-lease-duration=40s` via controlplane config; restarted one replica -> watch for stability.

jon (sre): after those changes etcd commit latency dropped from 240ms -> 45ms, leader flips stopped, apiserver 5xxs fell back to baseline. controller queue drain rate improving.

amelia (eng-runtime): reverted the high concurrency flag on canary service to 120 rps. canary kept paused.

maria (oncall): still seeing some attach errors but reduced by 90%. leaving monitoring for 30m. will reopen ticket with root cause analysis: interactions between burst provisioning + controlplane IO during compaction/snapshot windows.

jon (sre): followups: 1) add a rate limit knob in the provisioner to smooth attach bursts, 2) schedule heavy etcd compaction outside peak rollout windows, 3) add alert for leader-change-rate > 3/5m.

kai (infra): cost note: smoothing will slightly increase short-term reserved capacity usage but saves emergency failovers. file a cost tradeoff note for finance if adopting.

maria (oncall): thanks all. I'll keep thread updated, moving to monitoring phase. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: incident created: INC-20260320-1074 (assigned to eng-sre).
